title: Architecture Management Regulations: Impact on Building a House
desc: What an architecture management regulation is, who issues it, what it says about houses, why houses in covered areas need a permit, and how to look it up.
summary: Architecture management regulations under the Architecture Law 2019: their content, issuing authority, effect on construction permits and house design, and how to look them up.
body: Many homeowners know only about zoning plans and overlook the architecture management regulation, a document that may set the paint color, materials, roof, and ground floor of a house. This article summarizes Architecture Law No. 40/2019/QH14 and Decree 85/2020/ND-CP.
1. What is an architecture management regulation, and who issues it?

The regulation is prepared for the urban areas and rural residential areas of a province or city. The provincial People's Committee develops it and submits it to the People's Council of the same level for approval before issuance (Clauses 1, 2 and 4, Article 14 of the Architecture Law). The regulation must be consistent with urban design, national technical regulations, and local cultural identity.
Architectural rules for the whole area and for specific areas and streets; areas to be given priority for renovation and areas with special management requirements (Clause 3, Article 14).
Rules on colors and building materials; requirements for a building's facade, roof, and ground floor; and management of housing architecture (Clause 2, Article 12 of Decree 85/2020).

In rural areas: houses are built according to the indicators in the approved rural construction plan; the regulation may be prepared separately or integrated into the commune's general plan (Article 13).
A list of architectural works of value and rules for their protection.

A detached house of fewer than 7 floors and under 500 m² of floor area is exempt from a permit only if it is not in the areas listed in Point g, Clause 2, Article 43 of the Construction Law 2025, which include areas that already have an architecture management regulation. In other words, where a regulation exists, the house still needs a permit; see Which detached houses are exempt from a construction permit?.
One of the conditions for granting a permit is that the building conforms to the plan or the architecture management regulation (Point b, Clause 1, Article 44).
Colors, materials, and exterior decoration must ensure good appearance and not harm vision, health, the environment, or traffic safety.
Detached houses in urban areas must fit the overall architecture of the area and suit natural and climatic conditions.
Rural houses should preferably inherit traditional architecture, use local materials, and suit living customs.

Building a work not in accordance with the architectural design approved or the construction permit is prohibited (Clause 5, Article 9); see the fines in Fines for building without a permit or contrary to a permit.
5. Houses on the list of architectural works of value

The owner may be considered for State support funds for protection and restoration but may not change on their own the exterior architectural form, structure, or grounds; if the work deteriorates, the owner must report it to the local authority (Clause 4, Article 13).
6. Where can you look up the regulation?

Within 15 days at the latest after issuance, the whole regulation must be publicly announced, including by posting on the website of the provincial People's Committee or the authority that prepared it (Article 11 of Decree 85/2020). The regulation is reviewed every 5 years or on an ad hoc basis to adjust it (Article 15 of the Architecture Law). Before designing, ask the construction unit of the commune or ward People's Committee whether the plot lies within the scope of a regulation.

This article is a summary for reference only and does not replace legal documents. The Architecture Law 2019 and Decree 85/2020/ND-CP are partially no longer in force; Decree 85/2020 has been amended, and the consolidated document 12/VBHN-BXD is not yet available in full in our library. Some rules on the authority to prepare and approve the regulation still refer to the district level, so current rules should be checked.
